title: bee — how the library works
subtitle: A reusable product team made of skills. Write one prompt, get research, design, code, docs, and this kind of page.
audience: Anyone using or extending the library

summary.oneLiner: Say **"build blobby"** and the `product-builder` skill runs a fixed pipeline of specialist skills that hand off through files in `.forge/blobby/`.
bullets: **9 skills**: 1 orchestrator for new products, 1 for changes to existing apps, 6 specialist stages, and 1 learning loop
**4 subagents** so research and build slices can run in parallel
**One workspace contract** (`.forge/`) so any stage can be resumed, re-run, or done by another agent
Ends with an **interactive explainer** like this page, rendered from JSON

features.name: product-builder
features.what: Orchestrates idea → research → competitors → design → build → docs → explainer.
features.why: So you never re-write the 'how to build a product' prompt.

features.name: feature-change
features.what: Lighter pipeline for existing apps: recon → design → build → docs → explainer.
features.why: Changes need codebase understanding, not market research.

features.name: product-research
features.what: Users, pain points in their own words, demand signals, with cited sources.
features.why: Scope decisions should rest on evidence.

features.name: competitor-analysis
features.what: Landscape, feature matrix, complaints to exploit, a one-sentence positioning.
features.why: Copy what's proven; win where others fail.

features.name: product-design
features.what: MVP scope, flows, wireframes, tokens, data model, stack, build slices.
features.why: Gives the builder a spec it can follow without guessing.

features.name: feature-dev
features.what: Builds in verified vertical slices and keeps a build log.
features.why: Small verified steps; the log feeds docs and the explainer.

features.name: feature-docs
features.what: README, architecture, CHANGELOG from what actually exists.
features.why: Docs that describe the plan instead of the code are worse than none.

features.name: feature-explainer
features.what: Renders explainer.json into an interactive page (this one).
features.why: The last person only needs one page to understand the work.

features.name: skill-forge
features.what: Turns lessons and repeated workflows into skill improvements or new skills.
features.why: Borrowed from Hermes Agent: the library improves with every project.

walkthrough.title: 1. A skill is just a folder with SKILL.md
walkthrough.explain: The frontmatter `description` is what the agent reads to decide **when** to use the skill. The body only loads when it's used.
walkthrough.code:
---
name: product-research
description: Market and user research for a product idea ... Use as stage 1 of
  product-builder, or when the user asks to "research this idea", "is there a
  market for…", "validate my idea".
---

# Product Research
## Inputs
.forge/<slug>/00-brief.md
## Process ...
## Output: 01-research.md
walkthrough.why: This is the open SKILL.md format used by Claude Code and Hermes Agent, so the same folder works in both.
walkthrough.tip: If a skill isn't triggering, the description is almost always the problem. Add the phrases users actually type.

walkthrough.title: 2. The orchestrator chains skills through files
walkthrough.explain: `product-builder` holds the stage table and the gates. It calls each specialist and records progress in `STATE.md`.
walkthrough.code:
| # | Stage       | Skill               | Output file        | Gate |
|---|-------------|---------------------|--------------------|------|
| 1 | Research    | product-research    | 01-research.md     | —    |
| 3 | Design      | product-design      | 03-design.md       | user approves scope |
| 4 | Build       | feature-dev         | 04-build-log.md    | tests/build pass |
walkthrough.why: Files as hand-off make every stage resumable (`STATE.md`), reviewable, and runnable by a different agent.

walkthrough.title: 3. The explainer is data + template
walkthrough.explain: The agent writes `explainer.json`; `render.py` validates it and injects it into the HTML template.
walkthrough.code:
payload = (json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)
           .replace("</", "<\\/").replace("<!--", "<\\!--"))
html = TEMPLATE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
html = html.replace(PLACEHOLDER, payload, 1)
walkthrough.why: The agent spends its effort on content, not layout, and every explainer looks consistent.
walkthrough.tip: Escaping `</` stops a code snippet containing `</script>` from breaking the page.

walkthrough.title: 4. The learning loop
walkthrough.explain: After a run, lessons go to the right place: project CLAUDE.md, a patch to a skill, or a brand-new skill.
walkthrough.code:
| Specific to one project  | that project's CLAUDE.md |
| Improves a stage         | patch that skill         |
| New reusable workflow    | new skill folder         |
| One-off                  | nowhere                  |
walkthrough.why: Because install.sh symlinks, a patched skill is live everywhere immediately.

tryIt.step: Open Claude Code in an empty folder and say: `Use product-builder to build blobby, a tiny file-sharing app. Quick prototype.`
tryIt.expect: It writes `.forge/blobby/00-brief.md` and `STATE.md`, then starts research

tryIt.step: Approve the MVP scope when asked

tryIt.expect: A page like this one, about blobby

tryIt.step: In an existing app, say: `Use feature-change to add dark mode`

glossary.meaning: A folder with `SKILL.md` (instructions) and optional scripts/references/assets, loaded only when relevant.
A separate agent with its own context that the lead delegates a stage to, which allows parallel work.
The skill that decides stage order and gates: `product-builder` or `feature-change`.
The shared workspace folder where stages read inputs and write outputs.
A thin feature that works end-to-end (UI → logic → data) and can be demoed on its own.
A checkpoint the pipeline must pass, e.g. user approval or passing tests.

quiz.q: Why do stages hand off through files instead of the chat?
options: So any stage can be resumed, reviewed, or done by another agent
quiz.explain: Files make the pipeline restartable via STATE.md and let parallel subagents share work.

quiz.q: You want to add a feature to an existing app. Which skill?
quiz.explain: feature-change starts with codebase recon instead of market research.

quiz.q: Where should 'this repo uses pnpm, not npm' be saved?
quiz.explain: It's project-specific. Skills hold lessons that apply to every project.

limitations: Research quality depends on web tools being available in the session
The explainer loads Mermaid and highlight.js from a CDN, so diagrams show as text offline
nextSteps: Run it on a real idea and let skill-forge capture the first lessons
Add domain skills you reuse often (auth, payments, deploy, SEO)
